project: CRYPTO-22 — KeyPackage attestation (ephemeral MLS leaf ↔ DID leaf-binding) — umbrella #2187
description: CRYPTO-22 (#2187) replaces the non-standard MLS leaf==DID conflation with an ephemeral, context-scoped leaf signature_key plus an #active-signed KeyPackage attestation that binds all four leaf public keys to the member's DID (§9.7.1, §9.5.2; ADR-057 Amendment 2026-08-01). The program lands as slices S1–S7. S1 (the pure 0xFF03 data type + §9.5.1 serialization + §25.23 Vector 37 KAT) and S2 (the pure 13-check verifier core verify_attestation, checks 3–13, deliberately deferring the two resolution-dependent checks 1–2 to the runtime caller — merged as PR #2246) are already on main in crates/scp-mls/src/keypackage_attestation.rs. This PRD file is the CRYPTO-22 program home; it currently authors only S4. NOTE (observation, not authored here): S1–S3 shipped without PRD stories — a program-level provenance gap; those retroactive stories are out of scope for this artifact and are not fabricated here.

gates.name: Verifier resolve + current-key freshness seam (§9.7.1 checks 1–2)

stories.title: Implement the two caller-deferred KeyPackage-attestation verifier checks (§9.7.1 checks 1–2): a pure wasm-safe current-key + freshness seam in scp-mls (Layer A) and an async IdentityBackend-backed, Add-fail-closed seam in scp-runtime (Layer B)
stories.description: Implement the two verifier checks that the merged S2 pure core (verify_attestation, §9.7.1 checks 3–13) deliberately defers to the runtime caller — §9.7.1 checks 1 (the signing_key_id names the role the identity's key state lists #active and current; no other key verifies — rotation is revocation, §9.12) and 2 (the key state used to satisfy check 1 MUST be no older than MAX_ATTESTATION_KEY_RESOLUTION_STALENESS = 300s, §9.18.7 — a bound decoupled from and far tighter than the §9.10.7 privacy-cache TTL of 24h/7d). The merged S2 code documents this exact caller contract on AttestationVerificationContext::resolved_current_vm_pubkey and on verify_attestation's rustdoc ('This is what a later wiring slice (S4/S6/S7) MUST enforce before calling'). Build the seam in two layers, per the SCP wasm-safe / async split (ADR-057). LAYER A (verify_attestation_with_resolution — pure, wasm-safe, TRIGGER-GENERAL, in the existing crates/scp-mls/src/keypackage_attestation.rs module; re-exported from crates/scp-mls/src/lib.rs alongside AttestationTrigger/KeyPackageAttestation): a deterministic side-effect-free function that, given the attestation, an ALREADY-RESOLVED key state (the type `09-security-model.md` §9.7.4.2's definitions define, which `IdentityBackend::resolve` returns inside a `ResolutionOutcome`), its resolution timestamp (resolved_at, Unix seconds), now (Unix seconds), and the trigger (Add or Update — so Layer A's Update path is already complete here: the last-known-good grace is a resolution-FAILURE concern, and Layer A performs no resolution), plus the remaining leaf/credential ground-truth fields — first enforces check 2 (reject with a typed staleness error when now.saturating_sub(resolved_at) > MAX_ATTESTATION_KEY_RESOLUTION_STALENESS), then enforces check 1 (extract the public key the credential's signing_key_id's role names, from the key entry that key state lists `Current` in that role — reject where the key state lists no key `Current` there, or lists one whose bytes differ), then constructs the AttestationVerificationContext with resolved_current_vm_pubkey set to that extracted current key and delegates UNCHANGED to verify_attestation for checks 3–13 (so a rotated-away key surfaces as the existing check-3 SignatureInvalid). Layer A does NO I/O, NO resolution, and NO clock read — resolved_at and now are caller-supplied, keeping it wasm-safe and reusable by the browser client. LAYER B (verify_add_attestation — async, in scp-runtime — ADD-ONLY BY CONSTRUCTION): a function that resolves the signer's key state via the canonical `IdentityBackend` of `03-identity.md` §3.10.10, which is the protocol's one resolution entry point (the real production backend — NEVER a NoOp/Stub/in-memory nullifier, per the no-dev-stand-in tenet and #2211), applies the §9.7.1 'Resolution failure policy' Add branch (a resolution FAILURE is a REJECT, fail-closed, with NO fallback to a stale cached key state), supplies check-2's resolved_at to Layer A as the clock time at which it performed that `IdentityBackend::resolve` call (so a freshly-resolved key state passes Layer A's freshness gate; Layer B reads only `resolve`, never a key-state-age field the shared backend does not yet expose), applies the narrow testing carve-out (a positive whitelist admitting ONLY a testing-created identity to skip relay resolution, gated behind #[cfg(any(test, feature="testing"))] so it is never present in shipped production artifacts — mirroring the validate_creator_identity carve-out at crates/scp-runtime/src/crypto/mls/provider.rs), and delegates to the trigger-general Layer A. The async seam is deliberately narrowed to the Add case: verify_add_attestation accepts the Add's ground truth as a dedicated struct AttestationAddGroundTruth that carries the KeyPackage.init_key and has NO trigger field — Layer B constructs AttestationTrigger::Add { kp_init_key } internally, so an Update at this async resolver seam is UNREPRESENTABLE BY CONSTRUCTION (not merely undocumented). The Update async seam does not exist in S4; S7 builds it WITH the §9.7.1 last-known-good grace. The incomplete Update resolution-failure policy therefore cannot be reached from this story's code. Enforcement MUST NOT be keyed on any prefix of an identifier's textual form (§9.7.1 'Fail-closed scope'). SCOPE (startable now): Layer A plus the Add-fail-closed / current-key / testing-carve-out Layer B path are genuinely completable now against merged S2, using ONLY `IdentityBackend::resolve` and Layer A's caller-supplied resolved_at/now — they touch NO shared backend type. Two things are deliberately EXCLUDED as boundary-stable follow-ons, NOT hard ACs here: (1) resolver-side privacy-cache freshness enforcement — that a key state served from the §9.10.7 24h/7d privacy cache and older than MAX_ATTESTATION_KEY_RESOLUTION_STALENESS MUST force a fresh re-resolution — which requires the unsettled backend-freshness seam (open question a: `ResolutionOutcome` carries no resolution timestamp today, so Layer B cannot yet read a served key state's age) and is the tracked SCP-CRYPTO22-005 follow-on that depends on the shared #2211 resolver; and (2) the already-admitted-member Update last-known-good grace branch (§9.7.1 'Resolution failure policy', Update bullet) — DECIDED to land in S7, not S4: S4's async seam (verify_add_attestation) is Add-only by construction (AttestationAddGroundTruth has no trigger field), so the incomplete Update failure-policy is unrepresentable here rather than half-built. Excluding these keeps every hard AC implementable within the AC10 scope boundary (scp-mls + scp-runtime only; NEVER the crate that implements `IdentityBackend`). This story adds NO FFI export, NO ContextManager/Supervisor wiring, and NO pipeline_wiring.rs assertion — those are S6/S7. S1/S2 are already merged on main (S2 = PR #2246), so this story is startable with no blocking PRD story or GitHub issue — hence blockedBy/blockedByIssues are empty; there are no PRD story IDs to reference for S1/S2 (see the program-level provenance-gap observation in the PRD description).
acceptanceCriteria: Layer A is a pure, side-effect-free function added to crates/scp-mls/src/keypackage_attestation.rs whose signature takes an already-resolved key state, a resolved_at: u64, and a now: u64 (plus the remaining ground-truth leaf/credential inputs) and returns Result<(), _>; it performs NO async, NO network, and NO clock read (grep confirms the function body contains no `.await`, no backend call, and no SystemClock/Clock::now usage), preserving scp-mls's wasm32 safety; a `cargo test -p scp-mls` unit test compiles and calls it (§9.7.1 checks 1–2; ADR-057 Amendment 'code seam').

Check-2 freshness boundary is pinned by scp-mls unit tests against MAX_ATTESTATION_KEY_RESOLUTION_STALENESS (§9.18.7, which states the boundary): a key state with now - resolved_at == 299 PASSES the freshness gate, and one with now - resolved_at == 300 and one with now one second before resolved_at are each REJECTED with the story's typed staleness error before verify_attestation is reached (§9.7.1 check 2).

Check-1 current-key rejection is pinned by scp-mls unit tests: (a) when the resolved key state lists no key `Current` in the role the credential's signing_key_id names, Layer A REJECTS with a typed current-key error and does NOT call verify_attestation; (b) when that key state lists the signing key in one of the three conditions other than `Current`, the delegated verify_attestation returns the existing AttestationVerifyError::SignatureInvalid (§9.7.1 check 1; §9.12 rotation-is-revocation).

Layer A enforces the check-2 freshness gate BEFORE the check-1 current-key extraction, which is before the delegated verify_attestation checks 3–13 — asserted by a test where a stale (301s) key state that ALSO has a valid current key still fails with the staleness error, never a checks-3–13 error (§9.7.1 checks 1–2 ordering).

Layer B (`verify_add_attestation` in crates/scp-runtime/src/crypto/mls/attestation_verification.rs, synchronous) reads the signer's key through the injected `KeyResolver` (`scp_protocol::context::governance::KeyResolver`): on the production path that is the supervisor's key resolver, and a supervisor without one refuses `invite_member` with `NotInitialized` before any verification. The module constructs no NoOp/Stub/InMemory resolver (no-dev-stand-in tenet; #2211). Amended 2026-10-18 under the N3 ruling (Option 1, 2026-10-11): the verifier reads the `KeyResolver` seam the receive path already uses, not `IdentityBackend`.

Add fail-closed on resolution failure is pinned by a scp-runtime test (`add_resolution_not_found_is_fail_closed_reject`): with an injected `KeyResolver` that returns `None` for the credential's identity and `signing_key_id`, `verify_add_attestation` returns `AttestationRuntimeVerifyError::ResolutionNotFound` and consults no cached key (no cache-fallback code path exists). The seam stays Add-only by construction: it takes an AttestationAddGroundTruth struct with NO trigger field and builds AttestationTrigger::Add { kp_init_key } internally, so an Update at this seam is unrepresentable (the Update seam is S7) (§9.7.1 'Resolution failure policy' — New member (Add)). Amended 2026-10-18 under the N3 ruling.

Layer B passes the resolved key to the pure core `verify_attestation` for checks 3–13 with `now` read from the injected scp_clock::Clock; a test (`resolved_rotated_key_drives_check3_signature_invalid`) asserts that an attestation signed by a key other than the one the resolver returns fails check 3 with `SignatureInvalid`, and a test (`resolve_success_fresh_current_key_ok`) asserts that a correctly attested KeyPackage passes. Layer B does not enforce §9.7.1 check 2: the `KeyResolver` exposes no resolution age, so the honest `resolved_at` this criterion formerly required moves to SCP-CRYPTO22-005 (open question (a)). Amended 2026-10-18 under the N3 ruling.

No testing carve-out exists: every signer, including a testing-created identity, is resolved through the injected `KeyResolver`, and enforcement reads no prefix of an identifier's textual form; a scp-runtime test (`did_test_and_did_key_are_resolved_like_any_other_identifier`) asserts that the resolver is consulted for each (§9.7.1 'Fail-closed scope (positive whitelist)'). Amended 2026-10-18 under the N3 ruling.

The pure S2 core is byte-unchanged: `git diff origin/main` shows NO modification to the body of `pub fn verify_attestation`, to AttestationVerifyError, or to the `mod tests` §25.23 Vector 37 known-answer tests (vector_37_signing_preimage_matches_spec / vector_37_signing_hash_matches_spec / vector_37_extension_body_matches_spec) in crates/scp-mls/src/keypackage_attestation.rs — S4 is additive to that module only (§9.7.1 checks 3–13 remain the unchanged pure core).

Scope boundary is enforced mechanically: `git diff --name-only origin/main` touches only crates/scp-mls/src/keypackage_attestation.rs, crates/scp-mls/src/lib.rs (the load-bearing `pub use` re-export of the new Layer-A symbols, matching the crate's existing convention for AttestationTrigger/KeyPackageAttestation), crates/scp-runtime/src/crypto/mls/* (the new Layer-B module + its mod.rs declaration), and this PRD file — and modifies NO file under crates/scp-identity/, NO file under crates/scp-ffi/, NO pipeline_wiring.rs, and NO sdk-capability-matrix.json (the backend-freshness seam is SCP-CRYPTO22-005; FFI export, ContextManager/Supervisor wiring, and the pipeline assertion are S6/S7) (ADR-057 Amendment — 'code … is the follow-on implementation PR').
actionItems: Read crates/scp-mls/src/keypackage_attestation.rs in full — the merged S2 caller contract on AttestationVerificationContext::resolved_current_vm_pubkey and verify_attestation's rustdoc — and crates/scp-mls/src/credential.rs::resolve_signing_key (extracts a public key by signing_key_id from a key state, the reuse point for check 1).

Add Layer A to crates/scp-mls/src/keypackage_attestation.rs: a pure fn taking (attestation, resolved key state, resolved_at: u64, now: u64, leaf/credential ground-truth), enforcing check 2 (the resolution is fresh under MAX_ATTESTATION_KEY_RESOLUTION_STALENESS, §9.18.7) then check 1 (current-key extract via resolve_signing_key; reject where the role lists no `Current` key, or lists one whose bytes differ) then delegating unchanged to verify_attestation. Add a typed staleness error variant/error type; do NOT edit verify_attestation, AttestationVerifyError, or the Vector 37 tests.
Add scp-mls unit tests: the 300/301 freshness boundary; absent-or-retired current-key rejection; rotated-key → SignatureInvalid; and the check-2-before-check-1-before-3–13 ordering test.

Add Layer B module crates/scp-runtime/src/crypto/mls/attestation_verification.rs and declare it in crates/scp-runtime/src/crypto/mls/mod.rs: an async fn that resolves via an injected `IdentityBackend`, applies the Add fail-closed policy (an `Err`, or a verdict carrying no key state, ⇒ typed REJECT, no stale fallback), supplies resolved_at = the injected clock's time at the `resolve` call to Layer A, applies the #[cfg(any(test, feature="testing"))] testing-created-identity positive-whitelist carve-out (mirroring provider.rs::validate_creator_identity), then delegates to Layer A. Do NOT touch the crate that implements `IdentityBackend` — the backend-side privacy-cache freshness enforcement is the SCP-CRYPTO22-005 follow-on (details.followOn), not this story.

Add scp-runtime tests: the backend returns an `Err`, or a verdict carrying no key state, on Add ⇒ REJECT with no cache fallback; a successful resolve hands Layer A a resolved_at within skew of now (honest, clock-derived); testing carve-out skips a testing-created signer and no other; and `IdentityBackend` is injected (no NoOp/Stub constructed on the production path).

Run local CI before pushing: `cargo clippy -p scp-mls -p scp-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test -p scp-mls`, `cargo test -p scp-runtime` (with DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH), and the scp-runtime check-*.sh gate set; confirm `git diff --name-only origin/main` matches the scope-boundary AC.

Leave the resolver-side privacy-cache freshness enforcement (details.followOn / SCP-CRYPTO22-005) and the Update last-known-good grace branch OUT of this story entirely — 004's Layer B derives resolved_at from the clock at the `resolve` call and never inspects a cached key state's age, so it needs no `ResolutionOutcome` age field and touches no shared backend type. Author SCP-CRYPTO22-005 only after open question (a) is settled.

sources.section: ## Amendment (2026-08-01): Ephemeral MLS leaf key + identity attestation (leaf-binding)

mergedPredecessors.S1: pure 0xFF03 data type + §9.5.1 serialization + §25.23 Vector 37 KAT (on main)

openQuestions: Backend-seam freshness-extension shape (awaits human confirmation): `ResolutionOutcome` (`03-identity.md` §3.10.10) currently carries NO resolution timestamp, so Layer B cannot yet read the age of a key state served from cache. Two additive options — (a) add a freshness bound to `IdentityBackend::resolve`, or (b) add a resolved_at field to `ResolutionOutcome` — both touch the shared #2211 backend seam and MUST be settled upstream before the backend-side privacy-cache freshness enforcement can be wired. Because this seam is unsettled upstream, that enforcement is NOT a hard AC of SCP-CRYPTO22-004 (which would otherwise contradict its own scope boundary); it is the SCP-CRYPTO22-005 follow-on below. SCP-CRYPTO22-004's ACs are scoped so they hold under either choice.
resolvedDecisions: Update last-known-good grace ownership — DECIDED: S7, not S4. Previously open (whether S4 or a follow-on owns the §9.7.1 Update last-known-good grace branch). Resolved by narrowing S4's async seam: verify_add_attestation is Add-only by construction (it takes an AttestationAddGroundTruth struct with NO trigger field and builds AttestationTrigger::Add { kp_init_key } internally), so no async Update entry point exists in S4 and the incomplete Update resolution-failure policy is unrepresentable rather than half-built. S7 builds the Update async seam together with the bounded §9.10.7 last-known-good grace (degrading toward the MAX_KEYPACKAGE_ATTESTATION_LIFETIME backstop under a rollback-capable attacker). The pure trigger-general Layer A (verify_attestation_with_resolution) already handles both triggers correctly because the grace is a resolution-FAILURE concern and Layer A performs no resolution.
details.followOn: SCP-CRYPTO22-005 (to be authored once resolver-freshness seam shape — open question a — is settled; depends on the shared #2211 resolver): resolver-side privacy-cache freshness enforcement — a key state served from the §9.10.7 24h/7d privacy cache whose resolution is not fresh under MAX_ATTESTATION_KEY_RESOLUTION_STALENESS (§9.18.7) MUST force a fresh re-resolution and MUST NOT satisfy the attestation current-key check (§9.7.1 check 2). Deliberately NOT authored here: it cannot be implemented within SCP-CRYPTO22-004's scope boundary because it requires editing the crate that implements `IdentityBackend` (the `ResolutionOutcome` age seam), which the unsettled #2211 upstream governs.
s6WiringRequirements: (a) 005 gate on the Add path. Until SCP-CRYPTO22-005 lands, the `KeyResolver` that `verify_add_attestation` reads exposes no resolution age, so §9.7.1 check 2 (the 300 s key-state staleness bound) is unmet on every path that calls it, including `Supervisor::invite_member`, which the 2026-10-11 override below wires now. Until then a key state the resolver serves from the §9.10.7 privacy cache can satisfy check 1 after a rotation, which weakens §9.12 rotation-is-revocation on the Add branch for as long as that cache entry lives; a cache hit is a resolution success, so the AC6 Add fail-closed policy does not cover it. SCP-CRYPTO22-005 adds the resolution age to the resolver seam and the 300 s gate to Layer B. Restated 2026-10-18 (D3): the earlier text required a mechanical gate against wiring before 005, and no such gate exists.

(b) Update async seam is S7-only. S6 MUST NOT introduce an async Update entry point; the Update-path async seam MUST be built in S7 WITH the §9.7.1 last-known-good grace. In S4 it is intentionally absent — unrepresentable by construction (verify_add_attestation's AttestationAddGroundTruth has no trigger field) — and S6 MUST NOT add a half-built Update seam lacking the grace.

(c) Non-nullifier resolver. The `KeyResolver` that `verify_add_attestation` reads is the supervisor's injected key resolver, never a NoOp/Stub/in-memory stand-in; a supervisor without one refuses `invite_member` with `NotInitialized`, and the verifier module constructs no resolver of its own. Restated 2026-10-18 (D3) over the `KeyResolver` seam.

(d) Add-trigger fidelity, structurally pinned. S6 MUST construct AttestationTrigger::Add { kp_init_key } from the REAL KeyPackage.init_key of the processing Add — so §9.7.1 checks 7–8 (the init-key binding + the RFC 9420 §10.1 init_key != encryption_key guard) cannot be skipped by a mislabeled or fabricated trigger. verify_add_attestation's AttestationAddGroundTruth carrying kp_init_key as a required field makes this a type-level obligation, but S6 MUST feed it the real KeyPackage value, not a reconstructed/placeholder one.

Override (2026-10-11, the N3 ruling, Option 1): there is one verifier, `verify_add_attestation`, rewritten in place over `KeyResolver`, and it is wired into the production Add path now, at `Supervisor::invite_member`, which verifies the invitee KeyPackage's attestation before it seals the invitation bundle (SCP-307; `05-contexts.md` §5.12.3.1). This overrides (a)'s requirement to wait for SCP-CRYPTO22-005 and AC 10's scope boundary. The other Add paths stay unverified and are filed as #2957; attestation at group creation and at every Update is #2959.
details.provenanceGapObservation: S1–S3 shipped without PRD stories (program-level provenance gap). Retroactively authoring those is out of scope for this artifact and is NOT fabricated here.
